summary: kuna decompile retries a by-name miss once with the DIV-20/DIV-68 non-x86-64 discovery bundle, so a discovery-generated name that kuna functions / kuna strings print is a name kuna decompile accepts. First attempt, and every invocation that already resolved, is byte-identical.

decisions.what: hypothesis and T_REFUTE mechanism both OVERTURNED; symptom upheld
decisions.detail: The filed hypothesis was 'the single-function name resolver uses a narrower symbol table'; T_REFUTE corrected that to 'sub_<hex> is a synthesized display name never registered as a symbol anywhere, so no table on the decompile path could contain it -- fold the name back to an address in kuna-cli'. Neither holds. sub_4045b0 IS a FunctionEntry name in ConsoleProgram::function_entries_canonical, and resolve_entry(Name(..)) resolves it: kuna decompile --json, kuna disassemble and kuna decompile-all all select the witness by that exact name on main today. Only the TEXT surface fails, because its decomp_dbg session never DISCOVERED the entry. kuna-cli's in-process drivers inject listing + funcstart_patterns + aif on a non-x86-64 image (load_program, DIV-20/DIV-68); build_script injected only `option listing on`. Bisected on the witness: listing alone still answers `no function matches`, listing + funcstart_patterns selects it. There is no name to fold and no table to widen -- there is an entry set to agree on.

decisions.what: why two testers filed what looked like two bugs
decisions.detail: The mode policy hid it. auto resolves to aggressive under 500 KiB and AGGRESSIVE_OVERRIDES names listing / funcstart_patterns / aif itself, so the gap is only reachable above the size threshold (KeyVal2.exe is 558,592 bytes -> reliable) or under an explicit --mode reliable. That is exactly the twin sighting 5bd1d1bb ('listed in auto mode, not selectable in reliable mode') -- same root cause, and the reason the two reports look unrelated.

decisions.what: plain alignment was implemented, measured, and REJECTED
decisions.detail: The obvious fix -- inject the same bundle up front, so the two surfaces share one policy -- was built and swept before shipping. It changes the ENTRY SET, and not every entry the bundle adds is real: on i386 and PPC64 the prologue matcher seeds a start a few bytes inside a function it already knew (PPC64 ELFv2's local entry point sits 8 bytes past the global one), and funcboundflow then truncates the outer function's flow at that seed. plt_ppc64le __do_global_ctors_aux went from a correct 354-byte do/while loop to an empty husk carrying only the funcboundflow warning; deregister_tm_clones, __do_global_dtors_aux and frame_dummy did the same, and i386_pie_nl register_tm_clones lost its body too. 8 such truncations over the 33 non-x86-64 fixtures, no other difference. Shipping that would have traded a selection bug for an output bug on the witness's own architecture.

decisions.what: shipped as a SECOND ATTEMPT, not as alignment
decisions.detail: The wider inventory is paid for only where it is the answer. decompile() splits driver_default_options into the Listing (always injected, exactly as before) and the discovery bundle (held back); a by-name selection the console answers with `no function matches` is retried once with the bundle appended. The retry is gated on a MISS -- not an ambiguity, not a load failure, not a pipeline abort, and never an --addr selector -- so every invocation that already resolved runs the byte-identical script it always ran, and the husk trade stays the whole-binary surfaces' to make, where a complete inventory is the point.

decisions.what: no option, no counters, no stages XML
decisions.detail: Tooling track. A retry that only fires where the command used to exit 1 cannot change emitted C for any run that worked, so there is no judgement call to put behind a phases.toml row: no options.rs registration, no catalog counter, no docs/options.md, no tests/stages case. No new DIV either -- this extends DIV-15/DIV-20/DIV-68, which are already recorded, and the counter:div lease is held by another builder this round.

collateral_sweep.method: kuna decompile --mode reliable <name> for EVERY name kuna functions reports, over all 33 non-x86-64 fixtures in kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures plus the witness KeyVal2.exe (250-name cap). The before arm is `--option funcstart_patterns off --option aif off`, which makes driver_default_options yield the Listing alone and the discovery list empty -- i.e. main's script, byte for byte, with no retry to make.
collateral_sweep.still_failing_note: macho_arm64e / macho_imports_arm64 `printf`, which names both the stub and the import slot. The selector model reports the ambiguity and its candidates rather than guessing, identically before and after; the retry deliberately does not fire on an ambiguity.
collateral_sweep.x86_64: unchanged by construction -- driver_default_options yields only the Listing there, so the discovery list is empty and there is no second attempt. Confirmed empirically on 40 x86-64 fixtures in the first (alignment) sweep: 0 differences.

not_closed: The non-x86-64 discovery bundle over-produces mid-function entries -- PPC64 ELFv2 local entry points and the i386 equivalent -- and funcboundflow then truncates the enclosing function to an empty husk. That is live on main TODAY in kuna functions and kuna decompile-all (plt_ppc64le __do_global_ctors_aux reports size 8 next to a sub_948 of 112) and is untouched here. It is an analyzer-tier defect and deserves a need of its own.

kuna decompile --addr and kuna decompile-all --addr still resolve the same address under different discovery configs on a non-x86-64 image, so they can render the same function differently. Pre-existing, and closing it means fixing the husk first.
A by-name miss on a non-x86-64 binary now costs two decomp_dbg runs before reporting `no function`. The error path got slower to be sure of itself; the success path did not.

cost.method: 3 interleaved runs each, wall clock, witness KeyVal2.exe (PE32 i386, 558,592 bytes)
cost.generated_name: 1.84-1.96 s, against exit 1 in 0.73-1.03 s before; the second attempt is a whole-program decode, the DIV-68 price kuna functions already pays on the same image

acceptance.promotion_note: verify --promote refuses: the recorded acceptance targets binary_source 'dataset' (KeyVal2.exe), which CI has no copy of. Vendored instead onto the in-repo entrymain_arm fixture -- a stripped ARM PIE whose sub_410 is discovered only by the bundle -- with the same command shape and --mode reliable, which is load-bearing at that size because auto would pick aggressive and supply the bundle itself.
acceptance.negative_control: with only the decompile.rs hunk reverted, the promoted probe FAILS and both new cargo tests FAIL; restored, all three pass.
